data.title: Pagination
data.tagline: Move through a large result set in separate pages
data.description: Pagination breaks a long result set into stable pages and works well when people need to return to a position or compare totals. Keep filters and sorting when the page changes. For a casual content feed, loading more items may feel more natural.

use: Data where total pages and position matter
avoid: Reset filters whenever the page changes
Use tiny page links that are hard to select
Show page numbers when the total is unknown
Paginate a short list that fits comfortably

lessonPractice.title: An audit log has tens of thousands of entries. People must share 'error logs, page 4' and return with filters preserved. Which browsing pattern fits?

options.label: Use pagination and keep the page number and filters in the URL
options.feedback: Stable pages support precise return and sharing, while URL parameters reproduce the same filtered result.

options.label: Load entries continuously without recording the current position
options.feedback: Continuous loading supports casual browsing but makes page 4 difficult to share or revisit precisely.

options.label: Turn each group of 20 logs into a numerically named tab
options.feedback: Tabs represent a small set of peer categories, not thousands of sequential result pages.

data.agentPrompt: Add pagination to the audit log and keep page number and filters in the URL. Preserve filters across page changes and restore the same result after refresh, back navigation, or sharing. Verify the first, middle, last, and empty pages.
